main_text.p: Productio est cum sonus producitur, vel du-plicatur, quod fit cum aliqua ex literis ي[?] vocali destitutis ideoque quiescentibus, immediatè vocalem sequitur. Fatha producitur ante ا[?] quiescens, ut [illegible, ~4 letters] xāp.[?] Damma ante و[?] quiescens, ut [illegible, ~4 letters] xŭp.[?] Kefra, ante ي[?] quiescens ut [illegible, ~4 letters] xŭp.

Sæpe ا[?] quiescens omittitur, & tunc Fatha præcedens est perpendicularis, ut ـ[?] vel hāc notâ (~) quæ Medda dicitur, supra literam usurpatur. Sic etiam Kefra ante ج[?] fit perpendicularis, ut [illegible, ~4 letters] judicium.
Pro ا[?] quiescente sæpe ponuntur و[?] & ي[?] cum ipsæ vocali carent, & notâ (ɔ) quæ Giesma dicitur, & immediatè eas præcedat Fatha, ut [illegible, ~4 letters] rama [illegible, ~4 letters] salâton.
Nunnatio est cum in fine dictionis duplicatur figura vocalis, quo fit ut ad proprium sonū adda-

page.notes: The Arabic examples are only partly legible at this scan resolution. Letters marked [?] are best readings, and whole Arabic words marked [illegible] could not be read with confidence. The transliterated words beside them (xāp, xŭp, judicium, rama, salâton) are as printed, though the Latin fragment "xāp" is itself uncertain. The stray dot at the lower left is not printed text and is left out. The Latin text is clear throughout.
